name: What is involved in restoring a neglected or foreclosed home's interior?

mainEntity.name: What is involved in restoring a neglected or foreclosed home's interior?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restoring foreclosed properties or long-neglected homes involves tackling compounded deferred maintenance before decorative work begins. Unlike standard remodeling, these projects frequently uncover hidden damage beneath surfaces, including rotted framing, compromised subflooring, abandoned wiring, damaged drywall, and outdated plumbing. The process begins with structural stabilization, debris clearing, and framing repairs. Next, licensed plumbing and electrical sub-trades bring mechanical systems into compliance. Only after the structural shell, subflooring, and rough-in trades pass verification does the crew finish the interior with new drywall, tile, finish carpentry, doors, trim, and fresh paint.
acceptedAnswer.description: Rehabbing neglected properties requires clearing debris, repairing structural framing and subfloors, coordinating trade rough-ins, and rebuilding with fresh drywall, tile, trim, and paint.
